intro.label: // ABOUT THE GAME
intro.title: What is Borrowed Shapes?
intro.paragraph_1: Borrowed Shapes is a 3D cooperative household adventure about a family trying to spend one meaningful Sunday together after years of drifting apart.
intro.paragraph_2: Players take the shapes of everyday objects representing David, Sarah, Alex, Lily, and their loyal dog Buddy. Each object has different strengths, speed, size, and weight, so every room asks the team to switch roles, plan together, and help one another.
intro.paragraph_3: The journey moves through familiar spaces such as the Kitchen, Bedroom, Bathroom, Basement, and Living Room. Simple household activities — cleaning, cooking, repairing, organizing, and finding a way forward — become cooperative challenges. After each room’s main tasks, the space shifts into a chaotic final challenge before the next door can be unlocked.

faq.q2: What should I do if I can't download the game?
faq.a2: Please check your internet connection, available storage on your device, and try downloading again from the Download page. If the download link has expired or is not working, return to the Download page to get a new link.
faq.q3: How do I report inappropriate content on the forum?
faq.a3: Please use the report function if available on the post or comment. The report will be sent to the moderation team for review according to community guidelines.
faq.q4: Where should I send gameplay feedback or new map suggestions?
faq.a4: You can create a post in the Forum with the Suggestion type or discuss it in community threads. Clear feedback with specific examples will help the development team evaluate it better.

1.title: 1. Introduction
1.content: The purpose of this Introduction is to demystify the Company's data processing practices and establish absolute transparency regarding what happens to personal information once it enters the ecosystem of Borrowed Shapes. The Player holds the fundamental right to be informed about data collection practices prior to engagement, while the Company has the legal responsibility under global frameworks like the GDPR and CCPA to publish an accessible, accurate policy. A practical scenario involves a privacy-conscious User reading this document to verify that their email address will not be sold to third-party marketing firms before they commit to creating an Account.

2.title: 2. Scope
2.content: This section defines the exact digital boundaries of the Privacy Policy. The policy applies exclusively to the Borrowed Shapes web platform, the multiplayer game client, the wiki system, and all associated back-end storage and routing services. The Player has the right to know exactly which digital properties are covered by these protections. The Company is responsible for ensuring data collected across all these internal platforms is governed uniformly. If a User clicks an external hyperlink on the community wiki that navigates to an unaffiliated third-party website, this clause clarifies that the Company's privacy protections sever at that point, and the third-party's rules apply.

3.title: 3. Definitions
3.content:
This clause provides strict legal parameters for privacy-related terminology to align with international data protection laws. The Player has the right to unambiguous language, while the Company has the responsibility to standardize its definitions4.
- Personal Data: Signifies any information that can directly or indirectly identify an individual, such as an email address, IP address, or specific hardware identifier.
- Processing: Refers to any automated or manual operation performed on data, including collection, storage, alteration, or deletion.
- Controller: Designates the Company as the legal entity deciding the purpose and means of processing Personal Data.
- Processor: Refers to third-party vendors (e.g., Cloudflare) acting on behalf of the Controller.

4.title: 4. Information We Collect
4.content:
This overarching section details the exact categories of data ingested by the system. The Company is legally responsible for practicing data minimization—only collecting what is strictly necessary to operate the game. The Player has the right to understand the complete breadth of their digital footprint within the ecosystem.
* Data Category | Specific Information Involved | Primary Purpose
* Account & Auth | Email, username, OAuth tokens, hashed passwords. | Identity verification and account access.
* Telemetry & Network | IP address, hardware ID, ping, packet loss. | Matchmaking optimization and anti-cheat.
* User Generated Content | Uploaded images, wiki text, avatar configurations. | In-game rendering and community features.
* Support & Security | Support tickets, reports, login timestamps, error logs. | Dispute resolution and infrastructure defense.

5.title: 5. Account Information
5.content: The policy requires the collection of basic identifiers to establish a persistent profile. The information involved includes the User's email address, chosen profile name, and account creation timestamp. The Company handles this by storing the data in secure, encrypted relational databases. The Player has the right to view and update this information in their profile settings. The Company is responsible for protecting this core data against unauthorized breaches and unauthorized internal access.

6.title: 6. Authentication Information
6.content: To secure Accounts against unauthorized access, the system processes authentication data. This involves cryptographic hashes of passwords (if standard email authentication is used) and active login session tokens. The Company hashes and salts all passwords, meaning the raw text is never known or stored. The Player has the right to securely reset these credentials at will. The Company must ensure session tokens expire appropriately to prevent session hijacking if a User logs in from a public computer.

7.title: 7. Google Login Information
7.content: When a User opts for third-party authentication for convenience, specific data is exchanged. The information involved is an OAuth 2.0 token and the verified email address provided by Google APIs. The Company handles this by validating the token with Google's servers to grant access. The Player has the right to revoke this connection at any time via their Google account security settings. The Company is responsible for not harvesting extraneous data from the User's broader Google profile beyond the basic authentication scope required for the game.

8.title: 8. Device Information
8.content: For engine optimization and security profiling, hardware data is collected upon client launch. This includes GPU specifications, operating system versions, and RAM capacity. The Company uses this telemetry to optimize the game's rendering pipeline and to detect hardware spoofing commonly associated with ban evasion. The Player has the right to understand that their hardware signature is logged. The Company must secure this data so it cannot be used by external actors to maliciously fingerprint a User across the wider internet.

9.title: 9. Browser Information
9.content: When the User accesses the web platform or wiki system, browser-specific details are logged. This includes user-agent strings, preferred language, and screen resolution. The Company uses this strictly for web layout optimization and automated anti-bot security checks. The Player's right to privacy here is protected by limiting the retention of this data. The Company is responsible for ensuring this data is aggregated and anonymized for broad analytics wherever possible, rather than tracking individual browsing habits.

10.title: 10. Network Information
10.content: To facilitate smooth online multiplayer experiences, network routing data is necessary. This involves latency metrics (ping), packet loss statistics, and regional routing hops. The Company utilizes this to connect Players to the most optimal regional servers and ensure fair competitive play. The Player has a right to a stable gameplay environment, which necessitates this background collection. The Company must not use network packet inspection to monitor or spy on data unrelated to the Borrowed Shapes game client.

11.title: 11. IP Address
11.content: The collection of Internet Protocol (IP) addresses is a fundamental requirement of internet communication. The IP address is collected during web browsing, authentication, and multiplayer matchmaking. The Company uses IP addresses for server geolocation, payment fraud prevention, and issuing network-level administrative bans. The Player has the right to utilize standard VPNs (if not expressly prohibited by the Terms of Service) to mask this, though it may degrade latency. The Company is responsible for treating the IP address as sensitive Personal Data under GDPR guidelines.

12.title: 12. Usage Information
12.content: In-game behavioral data must be tracked to improve the product and balance mechanics. This includes time spent in-game, specific features interacted with, and multiplayer lobby participation rates. The Company analyzes this telemetry to balance gameplay mechanics and identify popular features. The Player has the right to know their behavior is monitored for product development. The Company is responsible for utilizing this data solely for internal improvement and is strictly prohibited from selling it to behavioral advertising brokers.

13.title: 13. Analytics Data
13.content: Aggregated data helps the studio understand macro trends without identifying individuals. This involves converting individual usage statistics into broad cohorts (e.g., "15,000 players logged in on update day"). The Company handles this by mathematically stripping personal identifiers from the raw data before analysis. The Player has the right to object to certain types of direct tracking, though core aggregated analytics are generally exempt. The Company is responsible for ensuring third-party analytics tools comply with strict data protection agreements.

14.title: 14. Uploaded Images
14.content: The system allows visual customization, necessitating scalable image storage. The information involves the binary image files uploaded by the User for avatars or wiki pages. The Company handles this by uploading the files directly to Cloudflare R2 object storage10. The Player has the right to delete these images from their profile at any time. The Company is responsible for securing the Cloudflare R2 buckets, stripping sensitive EXIF metadata (such as GPS coordinates) from the image prior to public display, and monitoring for illicit content23.

15.title: 15. Wiki Contributions
15.content: The community wiki relies heavily on user-submitted text and structural edits. The information involves the text written by the User, permanently associated with their username and a timestamp. The Company handles this by publishing it to the public-facing web platform. The Player has the right to edit their contributions. The Company is responsible for maintaining revision histories to prevent vandalism and ensuring the public display of this data aligns with the moderation policies.

16.title: 16. Avatar Data
16.content: Visual representations of the Player are stored centrally on the servers. This includes the parameters of the avatar (e.g., color hex codes, geometric shape data, equipped items). The Company uses this data to render the character accurately in shared multiplayer spaces. The Player has the right to change their avatar configurations at will. The Company must ensure avatar data syncs rapidly across the Content Delivery Network (CDN) to ensure all players observe the correct representation with minimal latency.

17.title: 17. Reports
17.content: The moderation system relies on user-generated reports to maintain community standards. This involves the text of a complaint, the reporter's internal ID, and the accused's ID. The Company handles this in strict confidentiality, storing it in databases accessible only by the authorized moderation team. The Player has the right to submit reports securely without fear of public retaliation. The Company is responsible for investigating the data objectively and maintaining the absolute privacy of both the reporter and the reported individual.

18.title: 18. Customer Support Communications
18.content: When a User requests technical or billing help, communication records are generated. This includes emails, support ticket text, and any attached diagnostic screenshots. The Company stores this in its customer relationship management (CRM) software to track and resolve the issue. The Player has the right to request the closure and subsequent deletion of support tickets. The Company must ensure CRM access is heavily restricted internally to prevent unauthorized staff from reading private correspondence.

19.title: 19. Security Logs
19.content: To protect the backend infrastructure from malicious actors, security events are continuously logged. This involves tracking failed login attempts, rapid API requests, and anti-cheat heuristic triggers. The Company uses this data purely for defending the infrastructure and issuing automated bans. The Player has the right to be protected from platform-wide breaches. The Company has a legal responsibility to retain these logs for forensic analysis and threat intelligence in the event of a cyberattack.

20.title: 20. Information Collected Automatically
20.content: Certain background diagnostic data is ingested without active User input. This involves crash reports, error logs, and CDN routing requests generated when the game client fails. The Company automatically ingests this via the game client to fix software bugs and improve stability. The Player has the right to understand that the client operates these diagnostic tools. The Company must ensure that automatic crash dumps do not inadvertently capture or transmit sensitive files from the User's personal computer hard drive.

21.title: 21. Why We Collect Information
21.content: This section synthesizes the numerous collection points into clear, legally justifiable purposes. The Company must establish exactly why the data is needed to operate. The Player has the right to transparent reasoning regarding data utility. The Company collects information to operate the multiplayer servers, authenticate secure accounts, moderate the community wiki, provide customer support, and prepare the infrastructure for the future deployment of Virtual Goods. Without this data, the interconnected, online nature of Borrowed Shapes would entirely cease to function.

22.title: 22. Legal Bases for Processing
22.content:
This clause ensures compliance with the strict requirements of the GDPR and similar international legislative acts. The Player has the right to know the exact legal foundation upon which their data processing rests4. The Company bases its processing on the following pillars:
- Contractual Necessity: Processing emails and passwords is required to fulfill the Terms of Service.
- Legitimate Interest: Processing security logs, IP addresses, and game telemetry is necessary for the Company's legitimate interest in securing the platform and improving the product.
- Consent: Processing non-essential marketing emails or optional linked profile data relies entirely on the User's explicit, revocable consent.

23.title: 23. How We Use Information
23.content: This section bridges data collection and its practical application within the ecosystem. The information is utilized directly within the core game loop. The Company uses latency and IP data to match players into optimal lobbies, and utilizes avatar data to render the visual environment. The Player has the right to know their data is strictly used for game-related functionalities. The Company is responsible for ensuring that a database built for secure account authentication is never cross-pollinated with databases built for external advertising or data brokering.

24.title: 24. Sharing Information
24.content: This section identifies the specific circumstances where data leaves the Company's immediate physical or digital control. The Player has the right to know exactly who else touches their data. The Company is responsible for ensuring data is only shared with trusted, contracted third parties, law enforcement presenting valid subpoenas, or other players via public wiki profiles. The Company explicitly guarantees it does not sell Personal Data to third-party data brokers.

25.title: 25. Third-Party Service Providers
25.content: The Company employs specialized external vendors to operate the game at scale. The information involved includes cloud storage data and network routing metrics. The Company handles this by executing strict Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with these vendors. The Player's right to privacy extends seamlessly to these third parties. The Company is fully responsible for vetting these providers' security standards and ensuring they cannot use the data for their own independent purposes.

26.title: 26. Cloudflare Services
26.content: Borrowed Shapes relies heavily on Cloudflare for global infrastructure. The information involves CDN caching data, IP addresses for DDoS protection, and all user images uploaded to Cloudflare R2 object storage10. The Company handles this by routing traffic exclusively through Cloudflare's secure edge nodes. The Player benefits from significantly faster load times and enterprise-grade protection against network attacks. The Company is responsible for properly configuring the R2 buckets to ensure private data remains encrypted at rest10.

27.title: 27. Google Authentication
27.content: When a User links their Google account for seamless login, data is shared bidirectionally. The information involves cryptographic token validation requests sent from the Company to Google servers. The Company handles this via secure, encrypted API calls. The Player has the right to seamlessly log in using this integration without creating a new password. The Company is responsible for adhering to Google's strict API terms of service regarding user data handling and minimizing the data footprint.

28.title: 28. Analytics
28.content: To understand the player base and balance the game, data is shared with analytics software. The information involves aggregated telemetry, such as average session length and popular wiki pages. The Company handles this by anonymizing data before exporting it to the analytics dashboard. The Player has the right to not be individually profiled or tracked. The Company is responsible for ensuring the analytics provider cannot reverse-engineer the anonymized data back to a specific individual player.

29.title: 29. Fraud Detection
29.content: To prepare for future Virtual Goods, financial security is paramount. The information involves device IDs, IP addresses, and purchase attempts. The Company shares this with specialized payment gateways and fraud detection algorithms. The Player has the right to secure, protected financial transactions. The Company is responsible for utilizing PCI-DSS compliant partners to ensure sensitive credit card numbers are never stored directly on the game's native servers.

30.title: 30. Security Monitoring
30.content: To protect the integrity of the game and its users, security data is shared with cybersecurity vendors. This involves analyzing network traffic patterns to detect DDoS attacks, scraping bots, or brute-force login attempts. The Company utilizes automated tools to parse this data in real-time. The Player has the right to a secure, uncompromised gaming environment. The Company must ensure these monitoring tools respect data minimization principles and do not unnecessarily log benign user activity.

31.title: 31. Cookies
31.content: This section explains the use of local web storage technologies on the web platform and wiki. The information involves session IDs and authentication tokens stored directly on the User's browser. The Company uses strictly necessary cookies solely to keep the User logged in and secure the session against cross-site request forgery29. The Player has the right to clear these cookies at any time via their browser settings. The Company is responsible for not utilizing intrusive third-party advertising or tracking cookies without obtaining explicit, opt-in consent.

32.title: 32. International Data Transfers
32.content: This clause addresses the global nature of cloud computing and server hosting. The information involved encompasses all Personal Data, which may be transferred from the User's home country (e.g., within the European Economic Area) to servers located in the United States or other regions. The Company handles this legally by utilizing Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and frameworks like the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF)29. The Player has the right to know their data crosses international borders. The Company assumes legal responsibility for ensuring the destination country's processing facilities provide an adequate, legally compliant level of data protection.

33.title: 33. Data Retention
33.content:
This section establishes the precise lifespan of stored data to prevent permanent hoarding. The Company is responsible for not holding data perpetually once its purpose is fulfilled. The Player has the right to "the right to be forgotten."
* Data Type | Retention Period | Post-Deletion Handling
* Account Data | Duration of active account. | Deleted within 30 days of closure request29.
* Server Logs | 90 days. | Automatically purged after security analysis.
* Uploaded Images | Duration of active account. | Removed from Cloudflare R2 upon account termination.
* Financial Records | Up to 7 years. | Retained purely for statutory tax compliance.

34.title: 34. User Rights
34.content: This overarching section details the robust statutory rights granted to the User regarding their data, heavily influenced by global privacy laws. The Company is legally bound to facilitate these rights efficiently and without undue delay. The Player possesses the right to exert ultimate control over their digital identity and footprint.

35.title: 35. Access Requests
35.content: The Player has the right to request a complete copy of all Personal Data the Company holds about them. The information involves a compilation of account data, chat logs, and UGC. The Company handles this by providing a digital archive within 30 days of the verified request. The Company is responsible for ensuring the data is delivered in a readable, secure format without exposing the data of other users.

36.title: 36. Correction Requests
36.content: If data is inaccurate or outdated, it must be fixed. The information involves things like an outdated email address or a misspelled profile name. The Player has the right to rectify this information directly through the platform's UI or by contacting support. The Company is responsible for updating the central database and ensuring the correction propagates across the CDN and all connected services immediately.

37.title: 37. Deletion Requests
37.content: The Player holds the fundamental "right to erasure." The information involves all identifying account data and UGC. The Company handles this by permanently anonymizing the database entry and purging associated Cloudflare R2 image files. The Player exercises this right to sever their connection to the game entirely. The Company must comply, with the exception of specific data it is legally required to keep (e.g., financial records for tax purposes or hardware IDs linked to severe anti-cheat bans).

38.title: 38. Data Portability
38.content: The Player has the right to take their data elsewhere in a usable format. The information involves structured profile and telemetry data. The Company provides this via a standard, machine-readable format, such as a CSV or JSON file. The Company is responsible for ensuring the exported file contains the User's data without exposing the proprietary algorithms, database structures, or trade secrets of the game itself.

39.title: 39. Restriction of Processing
39.content: The Player can demand a pause on data processing under specific legal conditions, such as during a dispute over data accuracy or an unlawful processing claim. The information involves the temporary suspension of analytics processing or profile display. The Company handles this by freezing the account's data states. The Company is responsible for halting automated processing without outright deleting the data while the dispute is actively resolved.

40.title: 40. Children's Privacy
40.content: This section explicitly states the Company's strict stance on data collected from minors. The information involves preventing the ingestion of data from individuals under the age of 13 (or higher, depending on the specific local jurisdiction). The Company handles this via age-gating mechanisms during Account registration. The Player (and their legal guardians) have the right to demand the immediate deletion of inadvertently collected child data29. The Company is responsible for maintaining a zero-tolerance policy for the unauthorized collection of children's data and purging it instantly upon discovery.

41.title: 41. Security Measures
41.content: This clause details the defensive posture of the game's infrastructure. The information involves the protection of all databases, R2 buckets, and API endpoints. The Company handles this by deploying encryption in transit (TLS) and encryption at rest (AES-256) across all storage mediums10. The Player has the right to assume their data is treated with modern, enterprise-grade cybersecurity standards. The Company is responsible for conducting regular vulnerability assessments, penetration testing, and limiting database access strictly to essential engineering personnel.

42.title: 42. Incident Response
42.content: This section outlines the legal and technical protocol in the event of a cyber breach. The information involves the potential exposure of User credentials, emails, or profile data to unauthorized actors. The Company handles this by immediately isolating affected servers, patching the vulnerability, and assessing the scope of the leak. The Player has the right to be notified promptly if their unencrypted Personal Data is compromised. The Company is legally responsible for reporting the breach to the relevant supervisory authorities (e.g., the local Data Protection Authority) within 72 hours of discovery29.

43.title: 43. Policy Updates
43.content: This section allows the Privacy Policy to adapt to new legal regulations, international frameworks, or novel game features. The information involves the text and rules of this very document. The Company handles this by publishing a revised version on the web platform with a new, clearly visible "Last Updated" timestamp. The Player has the right to review these changes prior to continued engagement. The Company is responsible for notifying active Users via email or in-game prompts if the changes materially alter how their Personal Data is processed, requiring renewed acknowledgment.

44.title: 44. Contact Information
44.content: This final section provides a direct line of communication to the Data Protection Officer (DPO) or the dedicated privacy team. The information involves the email address or physical address of the Company's legal department. The Player has the right to submit privacy inquiries, deletion requests, or formal regulatory complaints. The Company is responsible for maintaining an active inbox at a designated address (e.g., privacy@borrowedshapes.com) and responding to all legitimate requests within statutory timeframes to remain legally compliant and accountable to its player base.

1.title: 1. Introduction
1.content: Rationale & Enforcement: This section exists to establish the foundational social contract between Borrowed Shapes and its players. We enforce this by treating it as the binding spirit of our community. Behavior & Examples: We expect players to read and understand these principles. Acceptable behavior involves actively applying these guidelines during gameplay. Unacceptable behavior includes ignoring these rules or claiming ignorance when caught violating them. Consequences: Ignorance of the Introduction will not prevent account sanctions.

2.title: 2. Community Values
2.content: Rationale & Enforcement: This exists to define our core pillars: creativity, fairness, and inclusion. Enforcement focuses on rewarding positive contributions and penalizing those who undermine the ecosystem. Behavior & Examples: Players are expected to foster a welcoming environment. Acceptable behavior includes helping new players navigate the wiki. Unacceptable behavior involves gatekeeping or discouraging others from participating. Consequences: Violating core values leads to progressive disciplinary action.

3.title: 3. Respect for Others
3.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Mutual respect ensures the platform remains enjoyable for millions of global players. We enforce this through proactive chat moderation and user reports. Behavior & Examples: Treat others with basic human dignity. Acceptable behavior is congratulating an opponent after a match. Unacceptable behavior includes personal attacks based on someone’s gameplay style. Consequences: Infractions may result in warnings or temporary communication suspensions.

4.title: 4. Inclusivity
4.content: Rationale & Enforcement: This exists to ensure Borrowed Shapes is accessible to everyone regardless of background. We enforce this via strict zero-tolerance policies for exclusionary behavior. Behavior & Examples: Players must welcome diverse individuals. Acceptable behavior includes inviting players from different regions to your community event. Unacceptable behavior is creating a future guild that explicitly bans players based on real-world demographics. Consequences: Exclusionary actions yield immediate temporary or permanent bans.

5.title: 5. Respectful Communication
5.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To keep public chat and wiki discussions constructive. Moderation relies on automated filters and manual review of reported text. Behavior & Examples: Communicate clearly and politely. Acceptable behavior includes debating game mechanics respectfully on the wiki. Unacceptable behavior includes excessive profanity or screaming in voice channels. Consequences: Chat restrictions or "mutes".

6.title: 6. Harassment
6.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Harassment degrades mental health and community safety. We employ a zero-tolerance philosophy for targeted abuse, utilizing chat logs for verification. Behavior & Examples: Players must leave others alone if requested. Acceptable behavior is engaging in light, mutual banter. Unacceptable behavior is stalking a player across lobbies or repeatedly sending unwanted messages. Consequences: Harassment bans escalate rapidly to permanent account removal.

7.title: 7. Bullying
7.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Exists to protect vulnerable players from coordinated intimidation. We investigate bullying claims by looking at patterns of behavior over time. Behavior & Examples: Support peers rather than tear them down. Acceptable behavior is offering constructive feedback on a user's uploaded avatar. Unacceptable behavior is organizing a group to mock a player's wiki contributions. Consequences: Temporary suspensions escalating to permanent bans.

8.title: 8. Discrimination
8.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To prevent bigotry within the game ecosystem. Enforcement is absolute and unyielding; discriminatory intent is heavily penalized. Behavior & Examples: Treat all real-world identities equally. Acceptable behavior is celebrating global real-world holidays in-game. Unacceptable behavior is treating someone differently due to their nationality or gender. Consequences: Immediate long-term suspension or permanent ban.

9.title: 9. Hate Speech
9.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Hate speech creates a hostile environment and violates international norms. We use automated detection and human review to enforce strict removal. Behavior & Examples: Abstain entirely from slurs and hateful rhetoric. Acceptable behavior is expressing pride in one's own heritage. Unacceptable behavior includes using racial slurs or promoting hate groups. Consequences: Immediate, non-negotiable permanent ban.

10.title: 10. Threats
10.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Real-world or digital threats compromise physical and psychological safety. We enforce this strictly and may report severe threats to law enforcement. Behavior & Examples: Never threaten harm. Acceptable behavior is saying "I'll defeat you in the next match." Unacceptable behavior is threatening to physically harm someone or hack their network. Consequences: Instant permanent ban and potential legal escalation.

11.title: 11. Violence
11.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To keep the platform focused on digital entertainment, not real-world harm. We actively monitor and remove any incitement to violence. Behavior & Examples: Keep conflicts strictly within the game mechanics. Acceptable behavior is defeating an opponent in a virtual match. Unacceptable behavior is encouraging others to commit acts of real-world violence. Consequences: Permanent removal from the Services.

12.title: 12. Sexual Harassment
12.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To prevent predatory and inappropriate sexual behavior. We enforce this through confidential reporting systems and rapid response. Behavior & Examples: Maintain a PG-13, non-sexual environment. Acceptable behavior is complimenting an avatar's aesthetic design. Unacceptable behavior includes making unwanted sexual advances or sharing explicit links. Consequences: Permanent account termination.

13.title: 13. Privacy Violations
13.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To protect players' real-world identities and data. Moderation prioritizes the immediate deletion of leaked personal information. Behavior & Examples: Respect the boundary between the game and real life. Acceptable behavior is calling a player by their in-game Username. Unacceptable behavior is sharing another player's real-life location or social media without consent. Consequences: Escalating bans and content removal.

14.title: 14. Impersonation
14.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To prevent fraud and protect the reputation of individuals and staff. We enforce this by verifying identities and stripping fake credentials. Behavior & Examples: Be yourself. Acceptable behavior is creating a unique persona for Borrowed Shapes. Unacceptable behavior is claiming to be a Borrowed Shapes developer or a famous streamer to deceive others. Consequences: Account locks or permanent bans.

15.title: 15. Doxxing
15.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Doxxing is a severe privacy breach used for intimidation. We treat this as a critical safety incident requiring immediate intervention. Behavior & Examples: Never compile or share real-world data. Acceptable behavior is keeping interactions anonymous. Unacceptable behavior is publishing a user's real name and phone number on the wiki. Consequences: Immediate permanent ban.

16.title: 16. Spam
16.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To keep communication channels functional and readable. We use automated rate-limiting to enforce this. Behavior & Examples: Communicate purposefully. Acceptable behavior is sending a single message looking for a group. Unacceptable behavior is pasting the same text 20 times in a global chat. Consequences: Temporary mutes and chat restrictions.

17.title: 17. Advertising
17.content: Rationale & Enforcement: The game is not a billboard for unauthorized commercial activity. We rely on community reports to flag rogue advertisements. Behavior & Examples: Keep conversations focused on the game. Acceptable behavior is linking to a relevant Borrowed Shapes wiki page. Unacceptable behavior is spamming links to an external shoe store or a cryptocurrency project. Consequences: Mutes, removal of content, or bans.

18.title: 18. Scams
18.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To protect the future digital economy and player trust. We track trade logs and chat history to identify deceptive patterns. Behavior & Examples: Engage in honest interactions. Acceptable behavior is completing a fair, agreed-upon future trade. Unacceptable behavior is promising to send real-world money in exchange for a Virtual Good and failing to deliver. Consequences: Permanent trade bans and account termination.

19.title: 19. Fraud
19.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To protect the financial integrity of the platform. We use payment gateway security and chargeback monitoring to enforce this. Behavior & Examples: Use legitimate payment methods. Acceptable behavior is buying premium currency with your own credit card. Unacceptable behavior is using stolen credit cards or initiating false chargebacks. Consequences: Immediate permanent account ban.

20.title: 20. Phishing
20.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To prevent account theft and data breaches. We actively block known malicious URLs and educate players on security. Behavior & Examples: Never ask for credentials. Acceptable behavior is directing players to the official login page. Unacceptable behavior is creating a fake website that looks like Borrowed Shapes to steal passwords. Consequences: Permanent account ban and network-level IP blocks.

21.title: 21. Account Sharing
21.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To maintain account security and ensure accurate matchmaking. We monitor hardware IDs and IP locations to detect sharing. Behavior & Examples: Keep your account to yourself. Acceptable behavior is playing on your own laptop. Unacceptable behavior is giving your password to a friend so they can complete a difficult challenge for you. Consequences: Account locks or suspensions.

22.title: 22. Cheating
22.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To preserve competitive integrity. We employ robust anti-cheat software (similar to industry standards) to detect memory manipulation. Behavior & Examples: Play the game fairly using authorized clients. Acceptable behavior is practicing to improve your skills. Unacceptable behavior is injecting code to create an "aimbot" or wallhack. Consequences: Immediate, irreversible permanent ban.

23.title: 23. Exploiting Bugs
23.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To prevent players from gaining unfair advantages via developer oversights. We evaluate whether the exploit was triggered intentionally or accidentally. Behavior & Examples: Report bugs rather than abuse them. Acceptable behavior is finding a glitch and submitting a support ticket. Unacceptable behavior is repeatedly using a map glitch to become invincible in multiplayer. Consequences: Stat rollbacks, temporary suspensions, or bans.

24.title: 24. Automation
24.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To ensure all actions are performed by humans, maintaining economic and competitive balance. We use behavioral analytics to detect non-human inputs. Behavior & Examples: Play the game manually. Acceptable behavior is using standard in-game hotkeys. Unacceptable behavior is writing a script to automatically farm resources while you sleep. Consequences: Permanent account ban.

25.title: 25. Bots
25.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Bots ruin server performance and inflate economies. We actively sweep for and ban bot networks. Behavior & Examples: Only human players are allowed. Acceptable behavior is playing the game yourself. Unacceptable behavior is running headless game clients to farm future premium currency. Consequences: Hardware bans and permanent account termination.

26.title: 26. Macro Usage
26.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Macros provide superhuman input speeds. We monitor input regularity to detect macro software. Behavior & Examples: One keystroke must equal one in-game action. Acceptable behavior is mapping a single action to a mouse button. Unacceptable behavior is using a macro to execute a complex 10-button combination instantly. Consequences: Warnings escalating to permanent bans.

27.title: 27. Toxic Behavior
27.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To prevent a culture of negativity that drives players away. We review reports of consistent negativity and poor sportsmanship. Behavior & Examples: Maintain a positive or neutral attitude. Acceptable behavior is playing quietly. Unacceptable behavior is constantly berating your teammates for making mistakes. Consequences: Communication restrictions and matchmaking delays.

28.title: 28. Griefing
28.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To stop players from intentionally ruining the experience of their allies. We use in-game telemetry (like friendly-fire stats) to verify griefing. Behavior & Examples: Attempt to win and collaborate. Acceptable behavior is playing poorly because you are new. Unacceptable behavior is intentionally blocking your teammates or sabotaging community projects. Consequences: Temporary suspensions.

29.title: 29. Unsportsmanlike Conduct
29.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To uphold the integrity of competitive play. Enforcement relies on manual review of severe match disruptions. Behavior & Examples: Play fairly and respectfully. Acceptable behavior is conceding a lost match gracefully. Unacceptable behavior is "rage-quitting" repeatedly or engaging in future match-fixing. Consequences: Competitive matchmaking bans and loss of rank.

30.title: 30. Username Policy
30.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Usernames are highly visible and must be appropriate for all ages. We use word filters and user reports to police names. Behavior & Examples: Choose a respectful identifier. Acceptable behavior is naming yourself "ShapeMaster99." Unacceptable behavior is using slurs, sexually explicit terms, or impersonating staff in your username. Consequences: Forced name changes or account bans.

31.title: 31. Display Name Policy
31.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Similar to Usernames, Display Names dictate the social atmosphere. We enforce standard filtering on all profile texts. Behavior & Examples: Keep it clean. Acceptable behavior is using your real first name. Unacceptable behavior is using bypass techniques to spell out offensive words. Consequences: Forced resets and temporary profile locks.

32.title: 32. Avatar Policy
32.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Visual representation must align with our safety standards. We review uploaded Cloudflare R2 images for inappropriate content. Behavior & Examples: Create fun, creative avatars. Acceptable behavior is uploading a drawing of a cat. Unacceptable behavior is uploading a graphic, violent image to map onto your character. Consequences: Image deletion and temporary account suspension.

33.title: 33. Profile Content
33.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Public profiles are visible to the community and must be safe. We moderate text and linked content on profiles. Behavior & Examples: Share your gaming interests safely. Acceptable behavior is writing a short bio about your playstyle. Unacceptable behavior is linking to external malware sites or adult content in your bio. Consequences: Profile wipes and community bans.

34.title: 34. Wiki Contributions
34.content: Rationale & Enforcement: The wiki is a collaborative educational tool. We enforce quality and safety through community moderation and revision history. Behavior & Examples: Contribute accurate, helpful information. Acceptable behavior is correcting a typo on a guide. Unacceptable behavior is vandalizing a page with spam or deleting useful articles. Consequences: Wiki editing bans.

35.title: 35. Comments
35.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Public comment sections must foster discussion, not hostility. We use automated filters for severe infractions. Behavior & Examples: Debate constructively. Acceptable behavior is disagreeing with a strategy. Unacceptable behavior is launching personal attacks in the comment section of a user's guide. Consequences: Comment deletion and posting bans.

36.title: 36. Player Collaboration
36.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Encouraging teamwork enhances the game's longevity. We promote positive collaboration and penalize sabotage. Behavior & Examples: Work together to achieve game goals. Acceptable behavior is sharing resources to build a structure. Unacceptable behavior is pretending to collaborate only to destroy the team's progress at the last second. Consequences: Reputation penalties and temporary bans.

37.title: 37. Guild Behavior
37.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Future guilds represent micro-communities that must still adhere to global rules. We hold Guild Leaders accountable for their group's culture. Behavior & Examples: Manage guilds responsibly. Acceptable behavior is kicking a toxic player from your guild. Unacceptable behavior is a Guild Leader orchestrating a mass harassment campaign against a rival group. Consequences: Guild disbandment and leader bans.

38.title: 38. Marketplace Conduct
38.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Future trading systems require absolute trust. We log all transactions to prevent fraud and exploitation. Behavior & Examples: Trade fairly. Acceptable behavior is bartering items at market value. Unacceptable behavior is using external software to artificially manipulate marketplace prices. Consequences: Permanent trade bans.

39.title: 39. Reporting Violations
39.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Reports are the lifeblood of our moderation system. We enforce a healthy reporting culture by acting on valid claims. Behavior & Examples: Report rule-breakers accurately. Acceptable behavior is utilizing the in-game tool to flag a cheater. Unacceptable behavior is ignoring severe toxicity instead of reporting it. Consequences: Ignored reports do not result in penalties, but using the system improves the community.

40.title: 40. False Reports
40.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Weaponizing the reporting system wastes moderation resources. We track report accuracy and penalize abusers. Behavior & Examples: Only report legitimate violations. Acceptable behavior is reporting a player you suspect of botting. Unacceptable behavior is organizing a group to falsely report an innocent player to trigger an automated ban. Consequences: Revocation of reporting privileges or account bans.

41.title: 41. Moderator Authority
41.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Moderators need the authority to maintain order. We enforce respect for moderator decisions to prevent endless arguments. Behavior & Examples: Respect staff instructions. Acceptable behavior is complying with a moderator's request to change the subject in chat. Unacceptable behavior is arguing with, insulting, or defying a moderator publicly. Consequences: Escalating bans.

42.title: 42. Warnings
42.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Education is our first step for minor infractions. Warnings serve as a documented chance to correct behavior. Behavior & Examples: Learn from mistakes. Acceptable behavior is acknowledging a warning for minor spam and stopping. Unacceptable behavior is ignoring the warning and continuing the exact same behavior. Consequences: Subsequent violations escalate to suspensions.

43.title: 43. Temporary Restrictions
43.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Enforced "cool-down" periods for repeated or moderate offenses. We enforce these automatically upon reaching a penalty threshold. Behavior & Examples: Wait out the restriction gracefully. Acceptable behavior is returning to play fairly after the ban expires. Unacceptable behavior is creating a secondary "smurf" account to bypass the temporary restriction. Consequences: Bypassing restrictions leads to permanent bans.

44.title: 44. Permanent Bans
44.content: Rationale & Enforcement: The ultimate penalty to protect the platform from severe threats. We reserve this for malicious, unrepentant, or illegal behavior. Behavior & Examples: Do not engage in zero-tolerance activities. Acceptable behavior is never encountering this screen. Unacceptable behavior is deploying malware, which guarantees permanent removal. Consequences: Complete loss of access, items, and platform rights.

45.title: 45. Appeals Process
45.content: Rationale & Enforcement: To ensure fairness and correct potential false positives. We enforce a structured review system for contested bans. Behavior & Examples: Appeal respectfully and with evidence. Acceptable behavior is submitting a support ticket detailing why a ban was an error. Unacceptable behavior is spamming social media or threatening staff to get an unban. Consequences: Abuse of the appeals process leads to appeal denial.

46.title: 46. Community Responsibility
46.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Everyone plays a role in keeping the game safe. We foster a culture where players proactively protect the ecosystem. Behavior & Examples: Lead by example. Acceptable behavior is de-escalating a tense chat argument. Unacceptable behavior is cheering on a toxic player. Consequences: Positive behavior yields a thriving game; negative behavior degrades the experience for all.

47.title: 47. Policy Updates
47.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Guidelines must evolve with the game. We enforce new rules only after they are published. Behavior & Examples: Stay informed. Acceptable behavior is reading the updated patch notes and rules. Unacceptable behavior is claiming a rule doesn't apply because it wasn't there last year. Consequences: Continued play constitutes acceptance of updates.

48.title: 48. Contact Information
48.content: Rationale & Enforcement: Provides an official avenue for policy questions. We manage this channel to provide clarity on complex situations. Behavior & Examples: Use official channels for support. Acceptable behavior is emailing support to ask if a specific wiki edit is allowed. Unacceptable behavior is using the contact form to submit spam. Consequences: Misuse may result in communication blocks.

1.title: 1. Introduction
1.content: Why it exists: To establish absolute clarity on what materials are permitted on Borrowed Shapes servers. Covered: All digital uploads, text, and media. Permitted: Original, safe content. Restricted: Content needing age-gating. Prohibited: Illegal or highly offensive material. Review/Decisions: Automated scanning and manual review based on strict guidelines. Appeals: Users can appeal removals via the support portal.

2.title: 2. Purpose
2.content: Why it exists: To protect the community and ensure legal compliance. Covered: The overarching philosophy applied to all user-generated content (UGC). Permitted/Restricted/Prohibited: Sets the baseline for all subsequent categories. Review/Decisions/Appeals: Guides moderators in ambiguous situations by prioritizing platform safety.

3.title: 3. Definitions
3.content: Why it exists: To remove legal ambiguity. Covered: Terms like "Content," "Upload," and "Prohibited." Permitted/Restricted/Prohibited: N/A. Review/Decisions/Appeals: Moderators use these strict definitions to standardize their enforcement logic.

4.title: 4. Content Ownership
4.content: Why it exists: To clarify intellectual property rights. Covered: The legal rights to UGC. Permitted: Original content owned by the user. Restricted/Prohibited: Stolen or infringing content. Review/Decisions: Moderators do not judge ownership unless a formal DMCA claim is filed. Appeals: Handled via formal legal counter-notices.

5.title: 5. User Responsibility
5.content: Why it exists: To make users accountable for their uploads. Covered: Everything submitted via the user's account. Permitted: Content vetted by the user before upload. Restricted/Prohibited: Uploading blind files. Review/Decisions: Moderators assume the account holder is responsible for the upload. Appeals: Users must prove their account was compromised if claiming they did not upload the prohibited content.

6.title: 6. Content Review
6.content: Why it exists: To explain the moderation pipeline. Covered: The processes of automated filtering (e.g., hash matching) and manual queue review. Permitted: Clean content passes through. Restricted/Prohibited: Flagged content is held. Review/Decisions: AI flags suspicious content; human moderators make the final call on complex cases. Appeals: Available if automation makes an error.

7.title: 7. Content Moderation
7.content: Why it exists: To establish the authority to remove content. Covered: The actions taken on flagged material. Permitted: Unaffected content. Restricted/Prohibited: Content subject to deletion, blurring, or warnings. Review/Decisions: Moderators act based on severity matrices. Appeals: Standard ticket appeals apply.

8.title: 8. Allowed Content
8.content: Why it exists: To encourage creativity. Covered: General benign media. Permitted: Original art, standard text, friendly discussions. Restricted/Prohibited: Anything violating specific bans below. Review/Decisions: Generally bypasses manual review unless reported. Appeals: Not applicable unless falsely flagged.

9.title: 9. Educational Content
9.content: Why it exists: To foster game knowledge. Covered: Tutorials, stats, and guides. Permitted: Factual, helpful game information. Restricted/Prohibited: Guides on how to exploit bugs or cheat. Review/Decisions: Community wiki editors and moderators vet for accuracy and rule compliance. Appeals: Wiki revision reversions can be appealed to head admins.

10.title: 10. Creative Content
10.content: Why it exists: To support the game's customization features. Covered: Custom avatars and shapes. Permitted: Original designs fitting the game's aesthetic. Restricted/Prohibited: Offensive or legally infringing designs. Review/Decisions: Image recognition software scans uploads for known offensive patterns. Appeals: Users can appeal rejected avatars.

11.title: 11. Fan Art
11.content: Why it exists: To celebrate the community's passion. Covered: User-drawn depictions of the game. Permitted: SFW (Safe for Work) art. Restricted/Prohibited: NSFW (Not Safe for Work) or hyper-violent depictions of game characters. Review/Decisions: Moderated based on visual content policies. Appeals: Standard process.

12.title: 12. Gameplay Images
12.content: Why it exists: To allow sharing of achievements. Covered: Screenshots and clips. Permitted: Standard gameplay capture. Restricted/Prohibited: Screenshots showcasing the use of cheat overlays or exploits. Review/Decisions: Reviewed when reported by other users. Appeals: Standard process.

13.title: 13. Wiki Articles
13.content: Why it exists: To build a centralized knowledge base. Covered: All text and structure on the wiki. Permitted: Lore, mechanics, and strategies. Restricted/Prohibited: Vandalism or off-topic rants. Review/Decisions: Peer-reviewed by the community; enforced by wiki admins. Appeals: Mediated on wiki discussion pages.

14.title: 14. Guides
14.content: Why it exists: To assist players. Covered: Long-form instructional content. Permitted: Legitimate game strategies. Restricted/Prohibited: Links to phishing sites disguised as "leveling guides." Review/Decisions: Link-scanning bots check external URLs. Appeals: Standard process.

15.title: 15. Community Projects
15.content: Why it exists: To govern large-scale user collaborations. Covered: Multi-user builds or events. Permitted: Inclusive, rule-abiding projects. Restricted/Prohibited: Projects designed to crash the server or exclude protected groups. Review/Decisions: Monitored by community managers. Appeals: Project leaders may appeal takedowns.

16.title: 16. Restricted Content
16.content: Why it exists: To manage content that requires context. Covered: Material that is not strictly illegal but requires gating. Permitted: Discussing mature themes within a historical lore context. Restricted: Requires warnings or age-verification. Prohibited: Crossing into explicit territory. Review/Decisions: Context-heavy manual review. Appeals: Case-by-case basis.

17.title: 17. Sensitive Content
17.content: Why it exists: To protect users from unexpected distress. Covered: Phobias, mild horror, or intense themes. Permitted: Spooky content fitting a Halloween event. Restricted/Prohibited: Hyper-realistic shock imagery. Review/Decisions: Moderators apply "safe for general audiences" tests. Appeals: Standard process.

18.title: 18. Misleading Content
18.content: Why it exists: To prevent community manipulation. Covered: Fake announcements or forged screenshots. Permitted: Clear satire or jokes. Restricted/Prohibited: Claiming to be official patch notes to crash the economy. Review/Decisions: Fact-checked against official studio communications. Appeals: Standard process.

19.title: 19. Commercial Content
19.content: Why it exists: To prevent the game from becoming an ad board. Covered: Solicitations, sales pitches, and branding. Permitted: Discussing a brand naturally. Restricted/Prohibited: Uploading corporate logos as avatars for unauthorized marketing campaigns. Review/Decisions: Moderators delete blatant advertising. Appeals: Standard process.

20.title: 20. Political Content
20.content: Why it exists: To maintain a gaming-focused environment. Covered: Real-world political campaigning. Permitted: Broad philosophical discussions. Restricted/Prohibited: Using the wiki to host real-world political manifestos or campaign ads. Review/Decisions: Removed when it disrupts the community. Appeals: Standard process.

21.title: 21. Religious Content
21.content: Why it exists: To prevent sectarian conflict. Covered: Real-world religious imagery and text. Permitted: Personal expressions of faith in a bio. Restricted/Prohibited: Proselytizing, denigrating other religions, or starting holy wars in chat. Review/Decisions: Contextual review focusing on disruption. Appeals: Standard process.

22.title: 22. AI Generated Content
22.content: Why it exists: To manage the influx of low-effort or legally gray material. Covered: Text or images created by LLMs or image generators. Permitted: Using AI to help draft a wiki outline. Restricted/Prohibited: Spamming the wiki with hundreds of unedited AI articles; uploading AI imagery that violates IP laws. Review/Decisions: Reviewed for quality and spam markers. Appeals: Standard process.

23.title: 23. Sponsored Content
23.content: Why it exists: To ensure FTC/legal compliance. Covered: Content paid for by external parties. Permitted: Disclosed sponsorships (e.g., a streamer event). Restricted/Prohibited: Undisclosed native advertising. Review/Decisions: We require clear disclosures; undeclared sponsorships are removed. Appeals: Standard process.

24.title: 24. Prohibited Content
24.content: Why it exists: To categorically ban dangerous material. Covered: The umbrella of zero-tolerance uploads. Permitted: None. Restricted: None. Prohibited: All items listed in subsequent prohibited sections. Review/Decisions: Immediate deletion upon discovery. Appeals: Highly restricted; only successful if proof of a false positive is provided.

25.title: 25. Pornographic Content
25.content: Why it exists: To comply with app store ratings and protect minors. Covered: Any visual or textual depiction of sexual acts. Permitted: None. Restricted: None. Prohibited: 100% prohibited. Review/Decisions: Automated NSFW image hashing and immediate manual bans. Appeals: Standard process (rarely overturned).

26.title: 26. Sexually Explicit Content
26.content: Why it exists: Broadens the pornographic ban to include highly suggestive material. Covered: Erotic roleplay, suggestive avatars. Permitted: Standard game models. Restricted/Prohibited: Modifying avatars to simulate sexual acts. Review/Decisions: Contextual review by moderators. Appeals: Standard process.

27.title: 27. Nudity
27.content: Why it exists: Maintains the PG-13 rating. Covered: Realistic depictions of human genitalia or bare chests/breasts. Permitted: Classical art representations in a strictly educational wiki context (rare). Restricted/Prohibited: Uploading nude selfies or explicit drawings. Review/Decisions: Immediate deletion. Appeals: Standard process.

28.title: 28. Child Exploitation
28.content: Why it exists: It is a severe international crime. Covered: CSAM, grooming behaviors, and sexualization of minors. Permitted: None. Restricted: None. Prohibited: Absolutely forbidden. Review/Decisions: Immediate account termination, data preservation, and reporting to authorities (e.g., NCMEC). Appeals: Not handled by standard support; requires legal intervention.

29.title: 29. Violence
29.content: Why it exists: To prevent real-world harm. Covered: Depictions or threats of real-world physical violence. Permitted: In-game fantasy combat. Restricted/Prohibited: Uploading videos of real-world assaults. Review/Decisions: Immediate removal and bans. Appeals: Standard process.

30.title: 30. Graphic Gore
30.content: Why it exists: To protect users from severe shock. Covered: Highly realistic depictions of mutilation or death. Permitted: Cartoonish, in-game damage. Restricted/Prohibited: Real-world accident photos or hyper-gory drawings. Review/Decisions: Automated visual screening and user reports. Appeals: Standard process.

31.title: 31. Self-Harm Promotion
31.content: Why it exists: To protect vulnerable individuals. Covered: Content encouraging suicide, cutting, or eating disorders. Permitted: Seeking mental health resources in support channels. Restricted/Prohibited: Glorifying or providing instructions for self-harm. Review/Decisions: Immediate removal; we may direct the user to crisis resources. Appeals: Standard process.

32.title: 32. Illegal Activities
32.content: Why it exists: We cannot host platforms for crime. Covered: Content facilitating or organizing illegal acts. Permitted: None. Restricted: None. Prohibited: Organizing theft, hacking, or trafficking on our servers. Review/Decisions: Investigation and removal, potentially reported to law enforcement. Appeals: Legal counter-claims.

33.title: 33. Drugs
33.content: Why it exists: To comply with global regulations. Covered: The sale, promotion, or glorification of illegal narcotics. Permitted: Discussing in-game "potions." Restricted/Prohibited: Using the wiki or marketplace to coordinate real-world drug sales. Review/Decisions: Immediate bans for distribution attempts. Appeals: Standard process.

34.title: 34. Weapons Promotion
34.content: Why it exists: To prevent the platform from becoming an arms marketplace. Covered: Content promoting the real-world sale or illegal modification of firearms and explosives. Permitted: Discussing historical weapons in a factual context; in-game weapons. Restricted/Prohibited: Posting 3D-printer files for firearms or linking to illegal arms dealers. Review/Decisions: Immediate takedown. Appeals: Standard process.

35.title: 35. Terrorism
35.content: Why it exists: Required by international law and basic morality. Covered: Content promoting, funding, or glorifying recognized terrorist organizations. Permitted: None. Restricted: None. Prohibited: Terrorist propaganda, recruitment materials, or manifestos. Review/Decisions: Immediate removal, permanent bans, and reporting to relevant authorities. Appeals: Handled via strict legal escalation.

36.title: 36. Extremism
36.content: Why it exists: To stop radicalization pipelines. Covered: Content promoting violent extremism not officially classified as terrorism. Permitted: None. Restricted/Prohibited: Hate group recruitment and violent radicalization materials. Review/Decisions: Expert trust & safety review teams handle these escalations. Appeals: Standard process.

37.title: 37. Hate Speech
37.content: Why it exists: Refer to Community Guidelines; this policy dictates the content removal. Covered: Slurs, racist imagery (e.g., swastikas). Permitted: None. Restricted/Prohibited: All hateful media uploads. Review/Decisions: Automated text/image filtering and strict manual bans. Appeals: Standard process.

38.title: 38. Harassment
38.content: Why it exists: To remove the artifacts of bullying. Covered: Images or text designed to demean a specific person. Permitted: None. Restricted/Prohibited: "Attack pages" on the wiki or uploading embarrassing photos of another user. Review/Decisions: Contextual review based on user reports. Appeals: Standard process.

39.title: 39. Threats
39.content: Why it exists: To remove dangerous intent. Covered: Text or imagery conveying an intent to harm. Permitted: None. Restricted/Prohibited: Death threats in comments or profile bios. Review/Decisions: Immediate deletion and ban. Appeals: Standard process.

40.title: 40. Defamation
40.content: Why it exists: To prevent legal liability and protect reputations. Covered: Provably false claims that damage a real-world entity's reputation. Permitted: Stating an opinion ("I don't like this streamer"). Restricted/Prohibited: Falsely accusing a real-world person of a crime on the wiki. Review/Decisions: Acted upon typically when a formal complaint is received. Appeals: Legal counter-notice.

41.title: 41. Privacy Violations
41.content: Why it exists: To remove leaked personal data. Covered: Real names, addresses, ID cards. Permitted: Sharing your own anonymous game stats. Restricted/Prohibited: Uploading a picture of someone's driver's license. Review/Decisions: Highest priority manual removal to contain the leak. Appeals: Standard process.

42.title: 42. Copyright Infringement
42.content: Why it exists: To comply with the DMCA and international IP laws. Covered: Unauthorized use of copyrighted media. Permitted: Content you own or have a license for. Restricted/Prohibited: Uploading a movie studio's proprietary characters as your avatar. Review/Decisions: Handled strictly via formal DMCA takedown notices. Appeals: DMCA counter-notices.

43.title: 43. Trademark Violations
43.content: Why it exists: To prevent brand confusion. Covered: Unauthorized use of registered logos or brand names. Permitted: Parody (where legally protected). Restricted/Prohibited: Naming your guild after a real-world corporation and using their logo. Review/Decisions: Actioned upon trademark holder requests. Appeals: Formal legal appeals.

44.title: 44. Pirated Content
44.content: Why it exists: To prevent the platform from hosting stolen software. Covered: Links to pirated games, movies, or music. Permitted: Discussing media legally. Restricted/Prohibited: Using the wiki to host torrent links for commercial software. Review/Decisions: Link removals and bans. Appeals: Standard process.

45.title: 45. Malware
45.content: Why it exists: To protect users' computer systems. Covered: Links or files containing malicious code. Permitted: None. Restricted/Prohibited: Uploading a "game mod" that actually contains a trojan virus. Review/Decisions: Automated security scanning of all files. Appeals: Standard process.

46.title: 46. Viruses
46.content: Why it exists: A specific subset of malware aimed at destructive infection. Covered: Executable files designed to harm systems. Permitted: None. Restricted/Prohibited: Distributing viruses via community uploads. Review/Decisions: Immediate deletion and permanent ban. Appeals: Standard process.

47.title: 47. Scams
47.content: Why it exists: To remove deceptive content. Covered: Text/images designed to steal credentials or money. Permitted: Legitimate game trading. Restricted/Prohibited: "Free Premium Currency" generator links. Review/Decisions: Rapid deletion of reported scam networks. Appeals: Standard process.

48.title: 48. Fraud
48.content: Why it exists: To remove content facilitating financial crimes. Covered: Instructions or links for credit card fraud. Permitted: None. Restricted/Prohibited: Selling stolen accounts via the marketplace. Review/Decisions: Permanent bans and deletion. Appeals: Standard process.

49.title: 49. Impersonation
49.content: Why it exists: To remove spoofed content. Covered: Profiles designed to look exactly like administrators. Permitted: Fan accounts (clearly labeled). Restricted/Prohibited: Using the official Borrowed Shapes logo as your avatar while claiming to be support. Review/Decisions: Forced profile resets. Appeals: Standard process.

50.title: 50. Spam
50.content: Why it exists: To remove junk content. Covered: Repetitive, low-value uploads. Permitted: Genuine community engagement. Restricted/Prohibited: Creating 50 identical wiki pages for SEO manipulation. Review/Decisions: Bulk deletion by moderators. Appeals: Standard process.

51.title: 51. Advertising
51.content: Why it exists: To remove unauthorized commercial content. Covered: Unsolicited marketing material. Permitted: None, unless officially partnered. Restricted/Prohibited: Uploading banner ads to the image servers. Review/Decisions: Deletion. Appeals: Standard process.

52.title: 52. Manipulated Media
52.content: Why it exists: To prevent disinformation. Covered: Deceptively edited images/video. Permitted: Clear memes and jokes. Restricted/Prohibited: Forging a screenshot of a player saying a racial slur to get them banned. Review/Decisions: Contextual review; penalties for falsifying evidence. Appeals: Standard process.

53.title: 53. Deepfakes
53.content: Why it exists: To protect individuals from non-consensual synthetic media. Covered: AI-generated faces/voices of real people. Permitted: None in a deceptive or harmful context. Restricted/Prohibited: Non-consensual deepfake pornography of real individuals. Review/Decisions: Immediate deletion and ban. Appeals: Standard process.

54.title: 54. Fake News
54.content: Why it exists: To stop the spread of malicious real-world disinformation. Covered: Coordinated disinformation campaigns. Permitted: Discussing current events. Restricted/Prohibited: Using the platform to run state-sponsored disinformation networks. Review/Decisions: Trust & Safety team escalations. Appeals: Standard process.

55.title: 55. Misinformation
55.content: Why it exists: To protect the integrity of game information. Covered: Deliberately false game info. Permitted: Honest mistakes on the wiki. Restricted/Prohibited: Maliciously rewriting a wiki guide to intentionally cause players to lose their items. Review/Decisions: Reverted by wiki admins; repeated offenses lead to editing bans. Appeals: Wiki dispute resolution.

56.title: 56. Profile Images
56.content: Why it exists: To regulate user representation. Covered: Static images uploaded for accounts. Permitted: SFW images. Restricted/Prohibited: Explicit or infringing images. Review/Decisions: Scanned at upload. Appeals: Standard process.

57.title: 57. Avatar Images
57.content: Why it exists: To regulate in-game visual representation. Covered: Textures and images applied to 3D avatars. Permitted: Creative, safe textures. Restricted/Prohibited: Applying offensive textures designed to bypass filters in 3D space. Review/Decisions: In-game reporting tools trigger reviews. Appeals: Standard process.

58.title: 58. Wiki Images
58.content: Why it exists: To regulate informational media. Covered: Diagrams, screenshots, and art on the wiki. Permitted: Relevant educational media. Restricted/Prohibited: Irrelevant shock imagery. Review/Decisions: Wiki admins manage and delete. Appeals: Standard process.

59.title: 59. Community Uploads
59.content: Why it exists: Covers general files and future features. Covered: Any data sent to Cloudflare R2. Permitted: Authorized game data. Restricted/Prohibited: Using our storage as your personal illegal file host. Review/Decisions: Backend monitoring of bucket sizes and types. Appeals: Standard process.

60.title: 60. Media Processing
60.content: Why it exists: To explain how we handle files technically. Covered: The stripping of EXIF data (like GPS coordinates) from uploaded images. Permitted: We process all files this way for safety. Restricted/Prohibited: N/A. Review/Decisions: Automated process to protect privacy. Appeals: N/A.

61.title: 61. Content Removal
61.content: Why it exists: To clarify that we hold final authority over our servers. Covered: The physical deletion of data. Permitted: N/A. Appeals: Standard process.

62.content: Why it exists: To explain "shadowbanning" or restricted views. Covered: Content that is hidden from public view but not deleted. Permitted: Content under active review. 66.title: 66. Permanent Restrictions
66.content: Why it exists: The final step for content policy violators. Covered: Permanent loss of specific privileges (e.g., permanently banned from uploading images, but can still play). Permitted: Playing the core game (if not fully banned). Restricted/Prohibited: Circumventing the restriction. Review/Decisions: Applied by senior moderators. Appeals: Highly restricted.

67.title: 67. Policy Updates
67.content: Why it exists: Policies must adapt to new types of content (e.g., new AI tools). Covered: Modifications to this document. Permitted: N/A. Restricted/Prohibited: Expecting old rules to apply to new updates. Review/Decisions: We will notify users of major changes. Appeals: N/A.
